title: CUDA-L1: Improving CUDA Optimization via Contrastive Reinforcement Learning

mechanism.populationDetail: A single performance-indexed database holds all successful RL-generated code samples in score buckets.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Score buckets organize all successful codes for prompt sampling, without elite-only admission or niche incumbents.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Successful code samples accumulate in an exemplar database; GRPO also updates model weights, outside candidate replacement taxonomy.
mechanism.generationDetail: The model emits a complete optimized implementation conditioned on a reference task and scored prior examples, without an editable selected parent.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Speed scores enter future contrastive prompts and GRPO rewards; executable/correct flags gate samples.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The two sampled codes are contextual exemplars, not true editable parents.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Gradient-based policy updates jointly optimize with a growing scored-code exemplar database, unlike fixed-model evolutionary population search.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/CUDA-L1 Improving CUDA Optimization via Contrastive Reinforcement Learning.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Currently cited only in a DeepSeek model-family table; six offline SFT generators plus a reward checker complicate model-count classification. Bucket exemplars are references, not parents; island sampling is only an ablation.
